description: §6.7.4 a `${ when @n changes { … } }` written inside an `<each>` row body is a registered effect, not dropped. One row; #inc bumps @n once, the effect bumps @hits once. Carried on impl#1 (S432, P7): the block is dropped from the row render ("empty logic interpolation skipped"), silently.
rationale: §6.7.4: "A `when` statement declares a reactive effect. The body executes whenever any listed dependency changes value." and "The body does NOT execute on initial mount." §6.7.2: every `${}` logic block is associated at compile time with the nearest enclosing element scope — an `<each>` row is inside the `<program>` scope, so the effect is live for the program's lifetime. With exactly one row the effect is registered once: no run at mount (@hits 0), one #inc → @hits 1.
